meta.notes: Control series: the energy decision is made in c and kept in d (summaries: c and d both 'will use a kinetic battery'). There is no serious challenge; the only doubt is missing cost information (B3).

chain.speaker: ID
chain.gist: The Industrial Designer proposes the kinetic energy source, where the user powers the remote by moving it.

chain.speaker: PM
chain.gist: The Project Manager summarises that kinetic power only needs the remote to be moved, unlike a battery that must be recharged or replaced.

chain.speaker: ID
chain.gist: The Industrial Designer says he has no costing information; the two workable front-runners are a standard battery or kinetic.

chain.speaker: ME
chain.gist: The Marketing Expert says kinetic watches are very handy because you do not even notice it.

chain.speaker: PM
chain.gist: The Project Manager concludes that the consensus is to use kinetic if at all possible.

chain.speaker: UI
chain.gist: The User Interface Designer raises the energy question again in the last meeting, asking whether it is kinetic.

chain.speaker: ME
chain.gist: The Marketing Expert says kinetic can be marketed as cost-saving and environmentally friendly.

chain.speaker: UI
chain.gist: Filling in the component sheet, the User Interface Designer confirms just kinetic.
